channel.title: The Minnesota Star Tribune - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Minnesota Star Tribune (startribune.com)

item.title: Are federal immigration agents held to same use-of-force rules as local police?
item.description: After an ICE agent fired shots during an arrest in St. Paul, experts explain how federal and local use-of-force rules compare.

item.title: How ‘Stranger Things’ landed ‘Purple Rain’ and gave it a big Gen Z boost
item.description: Prince’s hit had not previously been licensed for a movie or TV show.

item.title: Five extra points: Which young Vikings players are growing up, and which ones still need to?
item.description: After the Vikings’ season finale, we’re taking a look at the progress of five Vikings players who will be under 25 during the 2026 season.

item.title: What happens to Amy Klobuchar’s U.S. Senate seat if she runs for governor?
item.description: She would create a vacancy in Congress if she became governor, but Klobuchar could also stay in the U.S. Senate until after the November 2026 election.

item.title: Reductions in federally recommended childhood vaccines put Minnesota health officials in a bind
item.description: Ignoring leading professional medical associations, U.S. cuts pediatric vaccinations from 17 infectious diseases to 11.

item.title: Kaohly Her’s transition has had few surprises so far, but now the city attorney is out
item.description: Lyndsey Olson, one of the longest-serving members of former Melvin Carter’s team, is the first to announce her departure. Her has so far retained other St. Paul department heads.

item.title: Gophers football team adds receiver Perry Thompson, defensive tackle Naquan Crowder in portal
item.description: Thomas played the past two seasons at Auburn. Crowder will have two years of eligibility left with the Gophers.

item.title: Report: Hundreds more federal agents to arrive in Twin Cities for illegal immigration and fraud crackdown
item.description: CBS News reports the surge is expected to bring more agents to the Twin Cities metro, as Minnesota is under increased federal focus on fraud allegations.

item.title: Trump lands a knockout punch on Walz
item.description: Under attack from the administration, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz drops his bid for a third term.

item.title: Gov. Tim Walz abandons re-election bid as fraud scrutiny intensifies
item.description: Walz said that over the holidays he changed his mind about running again. He talked to U.S. Sen. Amy Klobuchar ahead of his announcement, and she’s said to be seriously considering the race.
